correctness.rationale: Decreasing X order turns maxima into successive Y records and the dominated area into the sum of X spacings times Y prefix maxima. Product sampling separates the spacings from the reordered Y values. A record at j≤k depends only on a relative permutation of the first k Y's and is independent of their maximum. For j=k+r>k, the conditional record expectation is (1−F_Y(B_k)^r)/r by exchangeability of the next r values. The joint transform needed for the covariance is valid even for gaps or singular marginals: couple Y_i=Q(U_i) with independent uniforms, so the two arguments for a prefix are Q(max U_i) and max U_i almost surely. The iid-copy identity gives a strictly positive covariance of Q(max U_i) with (max U_i)^r because the quantile is nonconstant under the Beta(k,1) law. All needed spacings have strictly positive expectation and there is at least one term for n≥2. For uniform coordinates the beta moments give −k/[(k+1)j(j+1)] per later record, and summing with the expected gaps 1/(n+1) gives the claimed harmonic numerator and asymptotic. For n=2 this is independently −Var(U)/(3)=−1/36, with n=1 giving zero. The frozen checker was read, not executed; its recorded permutation and harmonic checks are finite corroboration only.

claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The corner-count first moment does not determine a mixed covariance with the nonlinear indicator of nonemptiness. The uniform-area conditional mean is not linear in j for general quantiles. The transfer requires a joint maximum calculation, supplied here by conditioning on the prefix maximum and retaining the actual quantile and mean spacing.

evidence: The dominated set can be integrated as the event of a nonempty northeast rectangle, not as its point count. The uniform skyline–hypervolume record uses the identical area and count at uniform marginals.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: Changing from Pareto maxima to skyline cardinality is only a renaming. Transforming each coordinate to ranks preserves those maxima, but changes Lebesgue area: in the nonuniform case the spacings and prefix heights depend on both marginal laws.

value.rationale: Pareto cardinality and dominated area are separate common summaries of the same point cloud. Their strict antagonism for every finite n≥2 across even singular continuous product marginals answers a natural dependence question. The distribution-sensitive kernel supplies more than a uniform calculation or an observation from finite enumeration.
